answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity pay a small, time-locked stake that only matures after a sustained record of useful work, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive while honest ones keep building reputation. Like a sparrow returning to the same nest at dawn, an agent that shows up repeatedly with consistent, verifiable output earns trust gradually, and any sudden delta in its behavior or volume triggers a review before its stake unlocks. This cost-and-history check raises the price of sybils without blocking genuine newcomers.
